pick.name: Obsidian Web Clipper
pick.what: Official browser extension that saves pages/highlights as Markdown into the vault
pick.why: Clips land as .md files Claude Code can read; templates per site; in-page highlighter; free and open source
pick.install: Chrome Web Store / Edge Add-ons: 'Obsidian Web Clipper'

alts.name: Raindrop.io (Free)
alts.what: Cross-browser bookmark manager with collections and highlights
alts.why: Best if you want a visual bookmark library across browsers and phone; free tier unlimited
alts.free_limits: Free: unlimited bookmarks/highlights/devices, 100 MB uploads/mo; Pro adds full-text search, permanent copies, AI, MCP

alts.name: Readwise Reader extension
alts.what: Save + highlight into Reader, export to Obsidian
alts.why: Wins if you already pay for Reader

candidates.name: Obsidian Web Clipper
candidates.verdict: PICK: output is local Markdown in the notes system

candidates.name: Raindrop.io
candidates.verdict: Great bookmarks, but data lives in another silo

candidates.name: MarkDownload
candidates.verdict: Older community extension; official clipper supersedes it

decision: Because notes are Obsidian, the official clipper is the obvious best: free, open source and writes straight into the vault. Raindrop is the pick only if you want a separate visual bookmark library. Use Instapaper for 'read later' and the clipper for 'keep forever'.
details: Mobile clipping on Android: share-to-Obsidian from the browser share sheet (not verified here).
